messages:
Liam (FP&A): Heads-up: updated guidance for annual SaaS renewals + new pre-approved vendor list goes live Monday May 5. Please read before submitting renewal tickets.

Maya (Finance): Summary TL;DR: we want fewer urgent mid-cycle approvals and more predictable cash planning. Main changes: mandatory PO for any renewal > $5k/year, ability to flag vendors as 'pre-approved' to speed renewals under $15k, and clearer accrual instructions. Full doc: https://confluence.redwood/finance/saas-renewals-2026 :mag_right:

procurement-bot: New pre-approved vendor list published: 42 vendors. Reference ID: PREAPP-2026-05. :bookmark_tabs:

Olivia (Legal): Reminder: pre-approval does NOT bypass legal review for new contract terms or if vendor requests customer data access. Pre-approved status only speeds procurement & billing checks.

Nina (Security): Also add: any renewal that adds new integrations or inbound connections requires a short security checklist. We added a one-pager on the Confluence page.

Ravi (Eng): Quick question on PO timing: we often get an invoice before the PO is issued for renewal discounts. Can we still apply the discount if PO comes after invoice?

Maya (Finance): Good point. Policy: discount eligibility requires PO issuance before invoice date unless Procurement explicitly approves retro PO in the ticket with reason. Retro PO approvals will be limited and require justification + manager signoff.

Liam (FP&A): Accruals: for renewals booked in FY close windows, use the new accrual code ACCR-SUBS on the ticket and tag FP&A. This helps accurate runway reporting.

procurement-bot: Auto-checklist triggered when creating renewal ticket: attach last contract, current invoice, and renewal quote. Missing items = ticket returned.

Ravi (Eng): If a vendor is on pre-approved list but wants a custom SOW this year (one-off dev services), is that still accelerated?

Olivia (Legal): Custom SOWs = contract change, so no. Those follow standard >$15k review path.

Maya (Finance): Quick reference thresholds (effective May 5):
```
- <$1k/year: Team lead + procurement automated check (no PO required)
- $1k$5k/year: Dept finance approval + PO
- $5k$15k/year: Procurement review + PO. If vendor is pre-approved, procurement review time reduced (2 business days)
- >$15k/year: Procurement + Legal + FP&A review; possible exec notification
```

Liam (FP&A): FYI: we expect to route most lower-tier renewals to virtual-card payments when appropriate to reduce invoice processing. Use v-card for one-off renewals under $2k where vendor accepts card.

Nina (Security): Security checklist highlights: data access, SCIM/SSO changes, log retention. If any 'yes' answers, include security attestation in ticket.

Ravi (Eng): Noted. Can procurement-bot surface whether a vendor is pre-approved when we start a ticket?

procurement-bot: Yes 1: When a renewal ticket is created with vendor name, system responds with vendor status (pre-approved | requires-review) and list ID.

Maya (Finance): Action items: 1) Teams with >$50k/year SaaS spend — schedule a renewal calendar with Procurement by end of May. 2) All ticket creators: attach contracts & quotes up front to avoid return. 3) If you want a walk-through, drop preferred times here.

Ravi (Eng): We'll book a 30m slot next week.

Olivia (Legal): We'll circulate a short FAQ for SOWs vs renewals.

Liam (FP&A): Thanks all. This should clean up our month-end chaos. :slightly_smiling_face:
